title: Implied volatility needs context: 60% IV alone means nothing
summary: A score of 95 means little without knowing it is out of 100. In the same way, 60% IV can be high, low, rich or cheap. Beginners should at least use IV rank and IV percentile. The speaker compares IV with realized volatility instead: sellers want high IV and low realized movement.

steps.caption: This stock shows about 60% implied volatility. On its own, that number tells you little.
IV rank and IV percentile compare IV with its own past. That is some context, but not enough.
Realized volatility shows how much the stock really moves. This is the better reference.
IV minus realized: the context. A positive gap means sellers are paid more than the stock moves.
Best case for covered calls and cash-secured puts: high IV with a calm, low-volatility price.

takeaways: A raw IV number has no meaning without a reference.
IV rank and IV percentile are a minimum for beginners.
Compare IV with realized volatility; sell options when IV is high and realized movement is low.
caveats: VAY (volatility-adjusted yield) is the speaker's own metric, sold through his tools. It is unverified here.
